question.problem:
The signed curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{2}{\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}}}.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)={e}^{t},\,y(t)={e}^{-t}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =-{e}^{-t} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{″}(t) & ={e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(t) & =\frac{{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-(-{e}^{-t})\cdot {e}^{t}}{{(({e}^{t})^{2}+({e}^{-t})^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{1+1}{{({e}^{2t}+{e}^{-2t})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{({e}^{2t}+{e}^{-2t})^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
